newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan files rebuttal of U.S. claim on film at WTO.
newsitem.headline: Japan files rebuttal of U.S. claim on film at WTO.

text.p: The Japanese government has filed a rebuttal of U.S. complaints of unfair trade barriers in the photographic film industry with a World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel, a senior official of the Trade Ministry said on Thursday.

The rebuttal followed a U.S. complaint to the WTO's dispute settlement panel last month alleging that for the last 30 years Japan has imposed laws, regulations and administrative steps to strengthen its domestic industry and curtail opportunities for foreign firms.
"The U.S. argument is both factually baseless and legally groundless," the ministry official said, summarising the content of the rebuttal.
"Japan has never taken any action which is inconsistent with the GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) or any action which nullifies or impairs benefits under the GATT," he said.
The WTO is not expected to reach a decision on the dispute until October. The panel is expected to hold its next meeting in mid-April.
The U.S. has argued that the Japanese government attempted to thwart foreign entry into its photograhic film and paper markets through Japan's distribution system.

The rebuttal said: "The Japanese film and paper markets are open to imports... Empirical evidence shows that the government of Japan has not impeded the ablity of imported film to succeed in the Japanese market. Success in the Japanese market depends simply upon the efforts of private companies."
